title: The Office - Interview Skills 6 - Describing Ones Strengths
audio: mp3/250. The Office - Interview Skills 6 - Describing Ones Strengths.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Katherine.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳。

segments.en: And as you probably noticed on our website, this is one of many different parts of a series all about having an interview in English.
segments.zh: 正如你大概在我们网站上注意到的，这是一个关于用英语面试的系列，而这是其中许多部分之一。

segments.en: This is a job interview and at this point we're at about part 7.
segments.zh: 这是一个工作面试，目前我们大约在第 7 部分。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So today what we're going to talk about is the key question whenever you're having a job interview is they ask you to describe your key strengths.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们要谈的是工作面试中的一个关键问题：他们会让你描述自己的关键优势。

segments.en: And this is our word for vocabulary preview today so let's take a look at it.
segments.zh: 这是我们今天词汇预览的词，所以让我们来看看它。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预览。

segments.en: Okay, so you might have heard the word strength before.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你以前可能听说过力量这个词。

segments.en: This is something that you're good at.
segments.zh: 这是你擅长的事情。

segments.en: And so key strength or key strengths, plural, would be things that you think are most important about you as far as the things that you do well.
segments.zh: 因此，就你做得好的事情而言，关键的优势或关键优势，复数，将是你认为对你最重要的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So as we mentioned, your boss or your potential boss might ask you to describe your key strengths.
segments.zh: 正如我们所提到的，你的老板或你的潜在老板可能会要求你描述你的主要优势。

segments.en: So you're going to mention a lot of adjectives, positive adjectives saying how good of a worker you are.
segments.zh: 所以你会提到很多形容词，积极的形容词，说你是一个多么优秀的工人。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to our dialogue.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不听我们的对话。

segments.en: Let's see what Rebecca has to say about her key strengths and we'll look at those in a little bit.
segments.zh: 让我们看看 Rebecca 对她的关键优势有什么看法，我们稍后会看看这些。

segments.en: Okay, Rebecca.
segments.zh: 好的，丽贝卡。

segments.en: Now you've given me a good idea of your work and academic background but what about you as a person?
segments.zh: 现在我对你的工作和教育背景有了较充分的了解，那你个人的性格和特点呢？

segments.en: How would you describe your key strengths?
segments.zh: 你会如何描述你的主要优势？

segments.en: Well Mr. Parsons, as I mentioned before, I'm someone who needs new challenges.
segments.zh: 好吧，帕森斯先生，正如我之前提到的，我是一个需要新挑战的人。

segments.en: I'm really focused and hardworking.
segments.zh: 我真的很专注，很努力。

segments.en: I think my academic results prove this.
segments.zh: 我认为我的学习成绩能证明这一点。

segments.en: Yes, true.
segments.zh: 对，确实如此。

segments.en: But how about other personal qualities?
segments.zh: 但是其他个人品质呢？

segments.en: Well I believe I'm a good team player but I can also work well independently.
segments.zh: 好吧，我相信我是一个优秀的团队合作者，但我也可以独立工作。

segments.en: I'm very enthusiastic and well, I hope my colleagues would agree, I'm fun to work with.
segments.zh: 我很有热情，和我共事也很愉快——希望同事们也这么认为。

segments.en: What would you say is your most positive quality?
segments.zh: 你认为自己最大的优点是什么？

segments.en: That's a tough question but I would have to say my passion.
segments.zh: 这是一个棘手的问题，但我不得不说我的热情。

segments.en: I'm really passionate about journalism and passionate about my career.
segments.zh: 我对新闻业充满热情，对我的职业充满热情。

segments.en: All right so she obviously has a lot of good key strengths.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以她显然有很多很好的关键优势。

segments.en: Why don't we analyze a couple of those on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 我们不妨在语言要点中分析其中几个。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So one of the first things that Rebecca mentions is that she's really focused.
segments.zh: 所以丽贝卡提到的第一件事就是她真的很专注。

segments.en: Okay, so this word focused, what does this mean?
segments.zh: 好吧，focused 这个词是什么意思呢？

segments.en: All right, so if a person is focused, basically you're saying that you concentrate on your work.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以如果一个人专注，基本上你是在说你专注于你的工作。

segments.en: That's right and someone who's focused might be very good in a noisy office or in a place that is full of distractions like you said because they don't stop their work and think about the noise or move around or go talk to people.
segments.zh: 没错，像你说的，专注的人在嘈杂的办公室或充满干扰的地方也能表现很好，因为他们不会停下来去想噪音、到处走动或找人聊天。

segments.en: Someone who is focused just sits down and can do a lot of work all at once.
segments.zh: 一个专注的人只是坐下来，可以一次做很多工作。

segments.en: That's right, so she describes herself as focused and hardworking.
segments.zh: 没错，所以她把自己描述为专注和努力。

segments.en: So hardworking means basically what it sounds like, that someone works very hard.
segments.zh: 所以努力工作基本上意味着它听起来像，有人非常努力地工作。

segments.en: That means they put in a lot of hours, they get their work done, they're really, really dependable.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们投入了很多时间，完成了他们的工作，他们真的非常可靠。

segments.en: That's right, so as you can see we use the word hardworking together.
segments.zh: 没错，正如您所见，我们一起使用勤奋这个词。

segments.en: So if you work hard, you don't say I work hard.
segments.zh: 所以如果你努力工作，你就不会说我努力工作。

segments.en: You can say that but if you want to use it as an adjective, you say I am hardworking.
segments.zh: 你可以这么说，但如果你想用它作为形容词，你说我很努力。

segments.en: The opposite of course would be lazy.
segments.zh: 相反的当然是懒惰。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, so we're focused, we're hardworking and she also said that she is a good team player.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们很专注，我们很努力，她还说她是一个优秀的团队合作者。

segments.en: Okay, this is a really key phrase here because it's something that employers, so people who are hiring new staff like to look out for because most jobs you don't work alone.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一个很关键的短语，因为雇主，也就是招新员工的人，特别看重这一点，因为大多数工作都不是一个人干的。

segments.en: You work with other people and so a team player is someone who works well in a group or works well with others.
segments.zh: 您与其他人一起工作，因此团队合作者是在团队中运作良好或与他人合作良好的人。

segments.en: That's right, so a team player, everyone wants to have a good team player working for their team, for their company.
segments.zh: 没错，所以作为一个团队合作者，每个人都希望有一个优秀的团队合作者为他们的团队，为他们的公司工作。

segments.en: And apart from being a good team player, you also want to be enthusiastic.
segments.zh: 除了成为一名优秀的团队合作者之外，您还想充满热情。

segments.en: That's right, so this means that you are interested in what you do, you are excited about it.
segments.zh: 没错，这意味着你对你所做的事情感兴趣，你对此感到兴奋。

segments.en: It's not like oh God, I have to do this report.
segments.zh: 这不像哦，上帝，我必须做这份报告。

segments.en: It's like oh wow, I get to do this report, I'm enthusiastic, I'm really interested, I'm going to put a lot of energy into it.
segments.zh: 就像哦，哇，我可以做这份报告，我很热情，我真的很感兴趣，我会投入很多精力。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So being an enthusiastic person not only can be about working, you can be enthusiastic about anything, about painting your house, about going on a trip.
segments.zh: 因此，作为一个热情的人不仅可以工作，还可以对任何事情充满热情，粉刷房子，去旅行。

segments.en: Exactly, enthusiastic.
segments.zh: 没错，热情。

segments.en: Alright and our last word for language, takeaway is also a good quality to have if you are passionate about what you do or what you're doing.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们语言要点环节的最后一个词，如果你对自己做的事充满热情，那也是一种很好的品质。

segments.en: So someone who is passionate about something really, really likes that thing.
segments.zh: 所以一个真正对某事充满热情的人，真的很喜欢那个东西。

segments.en: That means that they love to do it or love to see it.
segments.zh: 这意味着他们喜欢这样做或喜欢看到它。

segments.en: Passion is the opposite of not interested.
segments.zh: 激情与不感兴趣的相反。

segments.en: So you're really, really emotional and excited and interested in something.
segments.zh: 所以你对某件事真的很有感情、很兴奋、很感兴趣。

segments.en: That's right, so you are passionate about something.
segments.zh: 没错，所以你对某事充满热情。

segments.en: It comes from the noun passion, so you have a passion for painting, maybe you love to paint.
segments.zh: 它来自名词激情，所以你对绘画充满热情，也许你喜欢画画。

segments.en: So you're very passionate about painting.
segments.zh: 所以你对绘画充满热情。

segments.en: So a lot of great adjectives there to describe yourself in a good way.
segments.zh: 所以有很多很棒的形容词可以很好地描述自己。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue again and we'll be back with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我们不妨再听一遍对话，之后回来继续流利表达。

segments.en: Okay Rebecca, now you've given me a good idea of your work and academic background, but what about you as a person?
segments.zh: 好吧，丽贝卡，现在你让我对你的工作和学术背景有了一个很好的了解，但是作为一个人，你呢？

segments.en: How would you describe your key strengths?
segments.zh: 你会如何描述你的主要优势？

segments.en: Well Mr. Parsons, as I mentioned before, I'm someone who needs new challenges.
segments.zh: 好吧，帕森斯先生，正如我之前提到的，我是一个需要新挑战的人。

segments.en: I'm really focused and hardworking.
segments.zh: 我真的很专注，很努力。

segments.en: I think my academic results prove this.
segments.zh: 我认为我的学习成绩能证明这一点。

segments.en: Yes, true.
segments.zh: 对，确实如此。

segments.en: But how about other personal qualities?
segments.zh: 但是其他个人品质呢？

segments.en: Well I believe I'm a good team player, but I can also work well independently.
segments.zh: 好吧，我相信我是一个优秀的团队合作者，但我也可以独立工作。

segments.en: I'm very enthusiastic and well, I hope my colleagues would agree, I'm fun to work with.
segments.zh: 我很有热情，和我共事也很愉快——希望同事们也这么认为。

segments.en: What would you say is your most positive quality?
segments.zh: 你认为自己最大的优点是什么？

segments.en: Hmm, that's a tough question.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一个棘手的问题。

segments.en: But I would have to say my passion.
segments.zh: 但我不得不说我的热情。

segments.en: I'm really passionate about journalism and passionate about my career.
segments.zh: 我对新闻业充满热情，对我的职业充满热情。

segments.en: Alright so on Fluency Builder today we've picked out three key phrases.
segments.zh: 好吧，流利表达今天我们挑选了三个关键短语。

segments.en: Let's take a look at the first one.
segments.zh: 我们来看看第一个。

segments.en: When Rebecca said, I'm someone who needs new challenges.
segments.zh: 当丽贝卡说，我是一个需要新挑战的人。

segments.en: Okay so this structure, I'm someone who, is something that you hear a lot of and you can actually fill in the end of that sentence with a number of different phrases.
segments.zh: 好吧，I'm someone who 这个结构你经常能听到，而且句尾可以填上许多不同的短语。

segments.en: So in here we heard, I'm someone who needs new challenges.
segments.zh: 所以在这里我们听说，我是一个需要新挑战的人。

segments.en: We could also say, I'm someone who needs structure.
segments.zh: 我们也可以说，我是一个需要结构的人。

segments.en: Alright so we can also change the verb right from needs to, I'm someone who likes a challenge.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们还可以把动词换掉，从 needs 换成 I'm someone who likes a challenge。

segments.en: Or maybe Tracy is someone who requires a lot of attention.
segments.zh: 或者也许特蕾西是一个需要很多关注的人。

segments.en: Right, so this is a way to introduce a characteristic of yourself.
segments.zh: 是的，所以这是一种介绍自己特征的方式。

segments.en: So you're telling people something about yourself.
segments.zh: 所以你在告诉人们一些关于你自己的事情。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So moving on, we also saw that Rebecca said that she is fun to work with.
segments.zh: 接下来，丽贝卡还说过，和她共事很愉快。

segments.en: I'm fun to work with.
segments.zh: 和我共事很愉快。

segments.en: Okay so let's just treat this like a little fixed phrase.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们把它当作一个固定的短语来对待。

segments.en: We say this about people all the time.
segments.zh: 我们常常这样形容人。

segments.en: He's fun to work with, she's fun to work with, or this group is really fun to work with.
segments.zh: 和他共事很愉快，和她共事很愉快，或者和这个团队共事真的很愉快。

segments.en: They're all really fun to work with.
segments.zh: 和他们一起工作真的很有趣。

segments.en: So that means that it's not serious, that you really enjoy doing it.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着这并不严肃，你真的很享受做这件事。

segments.en: So it's a little fixed phrase that you can use to say that it's nice to work with Rebecca or that she's very, not serious, not a mean person.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个固定的短语，你可以用它来说和丽贝卡共事很愉快，或者说她很随和，不是刻薄的人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And finally we have a phrase at the end, Rebecca hears a question she thinks is very difficult, she calls it a tough question.
segments.zh: 最后我们在最后有一个短语，丽贝卡听到了一个她认为非常困难的问题，她称这是一个棘手的问题。

segments.en: And so a tough question is something that is very hard to answer.
segments.zh: 所以一个棘手的问题是很难回答的。

segments.en: That's right, she says, hmm, that's a tough question.
segments.zh: 没错，她说，嗯，这是一个棘手的问题。

segments.en: So she's basically acknowledging the fact that the question is difficult, a tough question.
segments.zh: 所以她基本上承认这个问题是困难的，一个棘手的问题。

segments.en: Now we can combine this word tough with other things.
segments.zh: 现在我们可以将这个词与其他事物结合起来。

segments.en: That's right, you can say it's a tough situation, that means it's a hard situation to handle.
segments.zh: 没错，你可以说这是一个艰难的情况，这意味着这是一个难以处理的情况。

segments.en: You could also say he's having a tough time, that means that right now in his life there are many things that are difficult for him.
segments.zh: 你也可以说他过得很艰难，这意味着在他的生活中，有很多事情对他来说很困难。

segments.en: And so tough means difficult or hard or unpleasant.
segments.zh: 所以 tough 意思是困难、艰难或不愉快。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So a lot of good stuff coming from Rebecca, mentioning all the positive things about her.
segments.zh: 所以很多好东西来自丽贝卡，提到了她所有积极的事情。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to her dialogue one last time.
segments.zh: 我们不妨再听最后一遍她的对话。

segments.en: Okay Rebecca, now you've given me a good idea of your work and academic background, but what about you as a person?
segments.zh: 好吧，丽贝卡，现在你让我对你的工作和学术背景有了一个很好的了解，但是作为一个人，你呢？

segments.en: How would you describe your key strengths?
segments.zh: 你会如何描述你的主要优势？

segments.en: Well Mr. Parsons, as I mentioned before, I'm someone who needs new challenges.
segments.zh: 好吧，帕森斯先生，正如我之前提到的，我是一个需要新挑战的人。

segments.en: I'm really focused and hardworking.
segments.zh: 我真的很专注，很努力。

segments.en: I think my academic results prove this.
segments.zh: 我认为我的学习成绩能证明这一点。

segments.en: Yes, true.
segments.zh: 对，确实如此。

segments.en: But how about other personal qualities?
segments.zh: 但是其他个人品质呢？

segments.en: Well I believe I'm a good team player, but I can also work well independently.
segments.zh: 好吧，我相信我是一个优秀的团队合作者，但我也可以独立工作。

segments.en: I'm very enthusiastic and, well, I hope my colleagues would agree, I'm fun to work with.
segments.zh: 我非常热情，而且，我希望同事们也会认同，和我共事很愉快。

segments.en: What would you say is your most positive quality?
segments.zh: 你认为自己最大的优点是什么？

segments.en: Hmm, that's a tough question.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一个棘手的问题。

segments.en: But I would have to say my passion.
segments.zh: 但我不得不说我的热情。

segments.en: I'm really passionate about journalism and passionate about my career.
segments.zh: 我对新闻业充满热情，对我的职业充满热情。

segments.en: Alright so talking about key strengths, I think it's always difficult to talk about yourself and still sound a little bit humble, right, to not sound arrogant like saying I'm the best.
segments.zh: 好吧，说到关键优势，我认为谈论自己总是很困难，而且听起来仍然有点谦虚，对，听起来不像说我是最好的那样傲慢。

segments.en: Right, well that's the key here I think.
segments.zh: 对，我觉得这就是关键所在。

segments.en: You want to say really good things about yourself because you're a salesperson and you're selling your personality.
segments.zh: 你想说说自己的优点，因为你是个推销员，在推销自己的个性。

segments.en: But at the same time you don't want to sound like a jerk.
segments.zh: 但同时你不想听起来像个混蛋。

segments.en: Like I'm the best, I'm so smart, I'm so clever.
segments.zh: 就像我是最好的，我很聪明，我很聪明。

segments.en: That's a little bit off-putting, it makes people uncomfortable.
segments.zh: 这有点令人反感，它让人们感到不舒服。

segments.en: So I think the trick is a balance.
segments.zh: 所以我认为诀窍是平衡。

segments.en: And I guess if you use words such as this, like you know, I'm focused, I'm hardworking, I'm independent, I have a passion for this.
segments.zh: 我想如果你用这样的词，就像你知道的那样，我很专注，我很努力，我很独立，我对此充满热情。

segments.en: It makes you sound like you're a really good worker but you're not arrogant, you're not saying oh well, you know, I'm the best of what I do or something like that.
segments.zh: 它让你听起来像是一个很优秀的员工，但并不傲慢，你不会说‘哦，你知道，我是这一行最棒的’之类的话。

segments.en: Right, so you're basically saying these are my skills but obviously I'm not the only person who has these great skills.
segments.zh: 对，所以你基本上是说这些是我的技能，但显然我不是唯一一个拥有这些伟大技能的人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay so that's all the time we have for today.
segments.zh: 好的，这就是我们今天所拥有的所有时间。

segments.en: Be sure to join us next week.
segments.zh: 下周一定要继续收听。

segments.en: We're also going to have kind of part two of this when we talk about our weaknesses.
segments.zh: 当我们谈论我们的弱点时，我们也会有第二部分。

segments.en: So this time we talked about our strengths, then we'll talk about weaknesses.
segments.zh: 所以这次我们谈到了我们的优势，然后我们将谈论弱点。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So we hope that you will check out our website EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 因此，我们希望您能查看我们的网站 Englishpod.com。

segments.en: If you have questions or comments, leave them there for us and we'll be in touch very soon.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题或意见，请将它们留在那里给我们，我们将很快与您联系。

segments.en: All right, we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好，到时候在那里见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
